group.js create sets id from resp.basic_group.id but server renders serialized group at top level without basic_group wrapper, so id never set and member-management UI doesn't render for freshly created group

adjudication.rationale: The client-side `Discourse.Group.create()` still sets `id` from `resp.basic_group.id`, but the server-side `Admin::GroupsController#create` continues to respond with `render_serialized(group, BasicGroupSerializer)`, exactly as it did before this diff. Since the previous client code (`createWithUsernames`) also read `resp.basic_group.id` and the response rendering call did not change shape in this diff, there is no verifiable mismatch introduced here. The diff does not show the server switching to an unwrapped top-level `{id: ...}` response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#create drops alias_level: client sends alias_level and UI shows combo-box for new groups, but create only assigns name and visible, so alias level is silently not persisted

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In the diff, the client now sends `alias_level` when creating a group: `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` includes `alias_level`, and `create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()` to `/admin/groups`. The admin group UI also still renders the alias level combo-box. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `name` and `visible` (and never reads/assigns `params[:alias_level]`). As a result, the chosen alias level for newly created groups will be silently ignored and the group will be created with the model/default alias_level instead of the selected value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#add_members silently succeeds for nonexistent usernames: unknown names are skipped and success_json rendered, and the client input isn't cleared, so admins believe users were added when they weren't

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members (added in the diff), usernames are split and each is looked up with User.find_by_username. Nonexistent usernames are simply skipped (no error/collection of failures). After the loop it calls group.save and renders success_json on success; if all usernames are invalid, the group is unchanged but the response is still success. On the client side, the addMembers action includes a TODO comment “should clear the input” and does not clear `usernames`, which can further contribute to misleading UX. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#remove_member reports success when removing a non-member: group.users.delete on a non-member id is a no-op and user_id is never validated, with no acceptance criterion or test
GroupsController#remove_member calls group.save after a HABTM delete, which is pointless since membership is already persisted, making the render_json_error branch unreachable

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then calls `group.save`. For a HABTM/has_many :through association, `delete` persists the join-table change immediately, so the subsequent `save` is indeed redundant. However, that redundancy is a minor inefficiency/code smell rather than a clear defect: `group.save` can still legitimately return false if validations fail (even if unlikely here), so the `render_json_error` branch is not provably unreachable from the diff alone. The finding overstates this as a real correctness problem.

GroupsController#members paginated response shape (members + meta: {total, limit, offset}) has zero test coverage despite the client depending on it and the endpoint being rewritten

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` to a new JSON shape: `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. The client-side `Discourse.Group#findMembers` is also changed to depend on `result.meta.total/limit/offset` and `result.members`. However, the only spec file modified/added in the diff is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, and it does not cover `GroupsController#members` at all (no request/spec asserting the new `members + meta` response contract). Based on the diff, this endpoint rewrite has no accompanying test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group-members page sets members asynchronously but the template binds against the model (group), which has no members until AJAX resolves, and the route no longer waits, so a slow/failed request renders a permanently empty members table with no loading or failure criterion

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying issue: findMembers/members loading became asynchronous and is no longer awaited/handled, so the controller/route renders before member data is available, leading to a race condition and potentially empty UI until/if the request resolves.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page has no pagination while backend hard-limits to 50 members, so groups with >50 members silently show only first 50 to regular users

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply pagination: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`, returning only that slice plus meta `{total, limit, offset}`. On the client side, the public group members route (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`) now just does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();` and the template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) iterates `{{#each m in members}}` (i.e., the `members` property set by `Group#findMembers`). There are no next/previous actions or pagination controls added for the public members page (unlike the admin group template, which adds next/previous UI). `Group#findMembers` defaults to `limit: 50, offset: 0`, so regular users will only ever see the first 50 members with no UI to access the rest when `meta.total > 50`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of get "users" route from admin groups collection breaks existing consumers of /admin/groups/:id/users with no replacement or mention in PR intent

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the member route `get "users"` under `admin/groups` (which would have provided GET `/admin/groups/:group_id/users`). However, the change set also introduces replacement functionality via new admin endpoints `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` (for modifying membership) and moves member listing to the non-admin endpoint `/groups/:name/members.json` (used by the updated `Group#findMembers`). The proposed finding claims there is “no replacement” and that it “breaks existing consumers”, but the existence of external consumers of `/admin/groups/:id/users` is not verifiable from the diff, and the “no replacement” portion is contradicted by the new endpoints and updated client code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only reformatting in admin-group-selector.hbs and user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs not traceable to membership-handling intent

adjudication.rationale: The changes in `admin-group-selector.hbs` remove leading/trailing blank lines, and `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` adjusts indentation/newlines inside `<a>` tags. These are whitespace/formatting-only edits that do not alter Handlebars expressions, HTML structure in a way that affects rendering, or any membership-handling logic. As such, the finding is a style/nit observation rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Extracted .form-horizontal label/input-width rules in admin_base.scss now scoped to .groups and .badges, causing scope drift and potential unintended visual changes on badges admin page

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move common `.form-horizontal` styling (bold labels, input widths, checkbox widths, spacing) out of `section.details .form-horizontal` and into a new `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }` block. That is a deliberate scoping change, but the proposed finding claims it causes “scope drift and potential unintended visual changes on badges admin page.” From the diff alone we cannot verify this is unintended or even a defect: `.badges` is explicitly included, so badges pages (if wrapped in `.badges`) would still receive these styles rather than lose them, and any “unintended” visual impact is speculative without evidence of badges markup or expected styling behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller_spec remove_member test sends PUT which routes to add_members, so the remove_member automatic-group guard is never actually tested and regressions would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the spec starting a `.remove_member` context with `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` while the routes map `PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` to `add_members` and `DELETE .../members` to `remove_member`. However this is a controller spec (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`), and `xhr :put, :remove_member` dispatches directly to the `remove_member` action (it does not go through route recognition and therefore does not “route to add_members”). So the claim that the automatic-group guard is “never actually tested” because it routes elsewhere is a misreading. (There may still be a separate issue that the spec uses the wrong verb relative to the real route, but that is not what the finding asserts.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6 addMembers has TODO to clear input and doesn't handle promise rejection, leaving stale usernames on failed add

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and explicitly includes `// TODO: should clear the input` but never clears/resets `usernames`, so the input will remain populated (“stale”) after attempting to add members. Also, `addMembers()` does not return the promise from `model.addMembers(...)` or attach any failure handling; any rejection is not handled in this action (verifiable from the diff).

Two sources of truth for member counts: meta.total uses live group.users.count while admin index uses stale user_count column, causing disagreement for groups with removed members (P1, confidence 75)

Unversioned breaking API change in create/update: request shape silently changed from nested group[name]/group[usernames]/group[visible] to flat top-level params, breaking existing API consumers (P1, confidence 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#create and #update to read flat top-level params (e.g., params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]) instead of the previous nested payload under params[:group] (e.g., params[:group][:name], params[:group][:usernames], params[:group][:visible]). The old code paths that accepted params[:group] were removed, and there is no backward-compatible handling for the nested shape. This will break any existing clients still sending the prior request format to POST /admin/groups or PUT /admin/groups/:id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH changes-based incremental add/delete endpoint deleted outright with no deprecation or replacement for non-UI callers of PATCH /admin/groups/:id (P1, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the PATCH-specific incremental membership logic (`update_patch`) and the `update` action no longer branches on `request.patch?`, so PATCH /admin/groups/:id with `changes[add/delete]` will no longer work. However, the diff also introduces replacement membership endpoints in the admin controller and routes (`PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` => `add_members`, `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` => `remove_member`). Because a replacement mechanism is present in the diff (even if it is a breaking change for existing PATCH callers), the finding’s claim of “no … replacement” is not verifiably true from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec test for remove_member issues a PUT, which routes to add_members in production routing; spec bypasses routing so DELETE member path and its automatic-group guard are untested (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb, the admin groups member-removal endpoint is declared as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` while `put "members"` routes to `groups#add_members`. In the spec diff, the remove_member test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which bypasses routing and uses the wrong HTTP verb compared to production (DELETE). This means the spec is not exercising the real route/verb wiring for member removal and would not catch a routing mistake (and it also misrepresents how the endpoint is called in production).

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers pagination totalPages = floor(user_count/limit)+1 is off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, rendering an empty member page (P3, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), this returns 3 instead of 2. The `next` action can then advance `offset` to exactly `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `Group.findMembers` will request `offset=100`, yielding an empty `members` list. `currentPage` becomes 3 and `showingLast` becomes true, so the UI will show a valid-looking but empty extra page. Correct logic should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (or equivalent).

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops nonexistent usernames and returns success_json even when zero requested users existed, making typo'd usernames silently swallowed (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. If a username doesn’t exist, it is simply skipped (no error collected). After the loop it calls `group.save` and returns `success_json` on success. If all provided usernames are nonexistent, no members are added but `group.save` will still typically succeed (no validations are triggered by “no-op” membership changes), resulting in a successful response that silently swallows typos/nonexistent usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member mutates join table via group.users.delete before gating on group.save with no transaction, so a validation failure returns an error over already-committed state change (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and only afterwards checks `if group.save` to decide whether to return `success_json` or `render_json_error(group)`. In Rails, `association.delete(...)` issues SQL immediately to remove rows from the join table; it is not deferred until `group.save`, and `group.save` does not roll that deletion back. Therefore, if `group.save` returns false (or raises) for any reason, the controller can respond with an error even though the membership removal already happened, and there is no transaction to keep the response consistent with persisted state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH-based incremental membership API (changes: {add, delete}) in admin/groups_controller.rb removed entirely with no deprecation path, breaking external consumers of PATCH /admin/groups/:id

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific incremental membership logic in `Admin::GroupsController` (`update_patch`, the `request.patch?` branch, and handling of `params[:changes][:add|:delete]`). The `update` action now only updates `alias_level`, `visible`, and (if not automatic) `name`, with no membership changes, while the route `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` would still hit `update`. As a result, external consumers sending `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes: { add, delete }` will no longer have their membership changes applied (and may even get a success response), which is a verifiable breaking behavior change introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: createWithUsernames / group creation with initial members removed; group creation no longer accepts usernames, forcing a two-step create-then-add flow and regressing the seed-members-at-creation feature

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the one-step “create group with initial members” path. On the client, `createWithUsernames(this.get('usernames'))` is replaced with `create()` and the `asJSON` payload no longer includes `usernames`. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#create` previously read `params[:group][:usernames]` and set `group.usernames = ...`; the new `create` only accepts `name` and `visible`. Additionally, the admin template only shows the “Add members” UI inside `{{#if id}}`, meaning you can’t add members until after the group is created. This forces a create-then-add two-step flow and removes the prior capability to seed members at creation time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing callbacks of group.remove(user) so groups.user_count is not decremented and becomes stale

adjudication.rationale: In the new Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code removes membership via `group.users.delete(user_id)`. Earlier in this diff, membership removals were done through `group.remove(user)` (see the removed `update_patch` implementation), which is likely where any bookkeeping/callback logic for group membership (including keeping `user_count` accurate) lives. Using the association `delete` on a has_many/through relationship removes join rows without running destroy callbacks on the join model, so any counter-cache or side-effect logic tied to those callbacks would be skipped, making `user_count` potentially stale. Nothing in `remove_member` compensates for that (it just calls `group.save`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec for remove_member uses xhr :put but the route is delete, so the request routes to add_members and the automatic-group guard in remove_member is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the route for member removal is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and the spec snippet indeed starts with `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. However, in Rails *controller specs*, `xhr :put, :remove_member` directly invokes the `remove_member` action with a PUT request; it does not go through routing and therefore will not “route to add_members”. As a result, the automatic-group guard inside `remove_member` would still be executed in that spec (assuming the spec is completed). The finding’s claim about routing to `add_members` and leaving the guard untested is not verifiably true from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller#members now unconditionally paginates all groups (including automatic ones) at 50, replacing prior behavior showing up to 200 members, with no pagination UI on the public group/members template

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the new code always applies limit/offset with a default limit of 50 for *all* groups: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. Previously, only `group.automatic?` was paginated (default 200) and non-automatic groups returned the full member list. On the client side, the public group members route (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6) now calls `model.findMembers()` once, and the public template (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs) merely iterates `{{#each m in members}}` without adding any next/previous controls. So the public members page will show only the first 50 members with no UI to reach the rest, which is a real regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded client-controlled `limit` on group membership enumeration in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb allows mass-enumeration/scraping of full member lists (membership-privacy regression); clamp limit to a max (e.g. 200)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no server-side maximum. This makes `limit` fully client-controlled and potentially extremely large, which can force large DB reads and large JSON responses (scraping/DoS vector). A clamp (e.g., `limit = [limit, 200].min`) is not present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unvalidated `offset` parameter allows negative values passed to .offset(), producing a 500 DB error; clamp offset to >= 0

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. If a client supplies a negative `offset` (e.g. `-10`), `to_i` preserves the negative value and ActiveRecord’s `offset(-10)` can raise (often `ArgumentError` / DB error), yielding a 500. There is no server-side clamp to `>= 0` in this method. Although the new JS client clamps offset before requesting, the endpoint itself remains vulnerable to negative values from other clients/requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin groups add_members does not normalize usernames before lookup (raw split of usernames string), so entries with whitespace silently fail to match

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming/normalizing `username`. If the incoming string contains whitespace around commas (e.g. "bob, alice"), the second token will be " alice" and `find_by_username` will not match, causing that entry to be skipped silently. This is directly observable from the diff and is a correctness defect in the added endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-existent usernames in add_members fail silently with a 200 response, resulting in silent partial success while the client reports success

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code splits the `usernames` string and for each entry does `if user = User.find_by_username(username) group.add(user) end`. Any non-existent username is simply skipped, and the action still proceeds to `group.save` and returns `success_json` (HTTP 200) if the save succeeds. There is no validation that all provided usernames existed or were added, so partial/no-op additions can return 200 and look like success to the client.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:104-107 uses xhr :put for remove_member but the route maps only DELETE, so the test exercises groups#add_members instead and never executes remove_member's automatic-group guard

adjudication.rationale: Although `config/routes.rb` maps `remove_member` to a `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` route, the spec line in question is a *controller spec* using `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. In Rails/RSpec controller specs, `process` dispatches directly to the named action (`:remove_member`) and does not “fall through” to another action like `add_members` based on routing. Therefore it will still execute `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` (including its `group.automatic` guard) even if the HTTP verb doesn’t match the route. The finding’s claim that it exercises `add_members` and never hits the guard is a misreading of how controller specs work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) which bypasses the user_count counter cache, leaving group.user_count stale and breaking admin UI count and members-list pagination, and the happy-path test never asserts user_count

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then `group.save`. For a typical `has_many :users, through: ...` association, `delete` removes join rows directly (often via `DELETE`/`delete_all`) and does not run the join model’s callbacks; if `groups.user_count` is maintained via a counter cache on the join model (which is consistent with the presence/usage of `user_count` throughout the diff and serializers), this path would not decrement the counter, and `group.save` won’t fix it. That would leave the persisted `user_count` stale for endpoints/serializers that read it (e.g., admin group listings), and the spec changes shown don’t add assertions around `user_count` to catch it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new client-side pagination model (findMembers, next/previous, totalPages, etc.) has no JS test coverage; totalPages = floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields 3 pages for exactly 100 users and next clamps offset to user_count causing an empty final page fetch
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate explicitly describes the same underlying pagination bug: clamping the next offset to user_count can result in an empty final page fetch when the total is an exact multiple of the page size (offset == total). It also notes totalPages miscalculation, but the empty-last-page issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten update action has no test for the non-automatic group update path (name rename, alias_level, visible); only the automatic-group name-ignore branch is covered

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, the new `context ".update"` only adds a test for the automatic-group behavior (name change ignored, visible updated). The prior tests that exercised updating a non-automatic group (renaming and membership updates via the old payload structure) were removed, and no new test was added to cover the non-automatic update path for `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` in the rewritten `Admin::GroupsController#update` (now reading top-level params, not `params[:group]`). This is directly verifiable from the diff: the only `.update` test is for an automatic group.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#update silently ignores the legacy `group: { usernames: ... }` parameter, so old cached clients' membership changes are dropped with a 200 response and no error (expand+contract violation)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` was changed from reading `payload = params[:group]` (and applying `payload[:usernames]`, `payload[:name]`, etc.) to reading only top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` (and it no longer processes usernames at all). If an older client sends the legacy nested payload `group: { usernames: ... }`, that parameter is ignored, and the method still calls `group.save` and returns `success_json` on success (200), so the membership change request is silently dropped. Note: the finding names `GroupsController#update`, but the issue is in `Admin::GroupsController#update` as shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#create reads top-level params[:name]/params[:visible] while old clients POST nested `group: { name, usernames }`, causing save failures or wrong payloads during the deploy window

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::GroupsController#create was changed from reading nested params[:group][:name]/[:usernames]/[:visible] to reading top-level params[:name] and params[:visible]. At the same time, the JS client was changed to POST top-level fields (Group#create now sends data: this.asJSON()). This is a breaking request-format change: a client still sending the old nested payload would result in params[:name] being nil, causing the controller to set group.name to an empty string and likely fail validation (or otherwise ignore provided nested values), i.e., wrong payload handling. The controller does not accept both shapes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#create removes ability to seed members at creation with no migration path, since old clients cannot add members (add_members requires an existing id)
remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing Group#remove and skipping bookkeeping like user_count counter maintenance and membership side effects

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member (new code), membership removal is done via `group.users.delete(user_id)` rather than using the Group API (`group.remove(user)`) that the same controller historically used for removals (see removed `update_patch` which called `group.remove(user)`) and that the new `add_members` action uses for additions (`group.add(user)`). Deleting through the association directly bypasses any logic in `Group#remove` (callbacks, counter/user_count maintenance, side effects), creating a correctness risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale denormalized user_count can cause blank or paged-off-end member lists in the new paginated UI and findMembers offset math

Removal of the old GET 'users' admin route in the same commit that switches the client to members.json leaves no dual-availability window; cached admin JS or external consumers hitting /admin/groups/:id/users get a 404 mid-rollout

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove an `admin/groups/:id/users` GET route (`get "users"`), but nothing in this diff shows the client (old or new) calling that endpoint. The updated client-side member loading uses `/groups/:name/members.json` (public GroupsController#members), not an admin `users` route. The finding’s main claim about a “dual-availability window” for cached admin JS or external consumers is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone (no evidence of any in-repo consumer of `/admin/groups/:id/users`).
